source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part II, Ch. 5 (Through the Eyes of Travellers).

sections.heading: 1. Travellers as Sources
points: Accounts of foreign travellers give valuable, outsider's insights into Indian society (roughly 10th–17th centuries).
Three important travellers: **Al-Biruni (11th c.), Ibn Battuta (14th c.), and François Bernier (17th c.)**.

sections.heading: 2. Al-Biruni
points: **Al-Biruni** — an 11th-century scholar from **Central Asia (Khwarizm/Uzbekistan)**; came with **Mahmud of Ghazni**.
Wrote the **'Kitab-ul-Hind' (in Arabic)** — a study of Indian religion, philosophy, sciences and society.
He noted the **caste system** and the 'barriers' that isolated Indian society; he compared Indian ideas with Greek and Islamic thought.

sections.heading: 3. Ibn Battuta
points: **Ibn Battuta** — a 14th-century traveller from **Morocco (Tangier)**; wrote the **'Rihla' (in Arabic)**.
Served **Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq** of Delhi as a **qazi (judge)**; later went to China.
Described Indian **cities (Delhi), markets, the postal system (dawa/uluq), coconut and paan, and the practice of sati**; found much that was **unfamiliar and exotic**.

sections.heading: 4. François Bernier
points: **François Bernier** — a 17th-century **French physician and traveller**; in India during **Shah Jahan/Aurangzeb**'s reign.
Wrote **'Travels in the Mughal Empire'**; **compared India unfavourably with Europe** (a comparative approach).

Argued (mistakenly) that there was **no private property in land** in India (crown ownership), which he linked to poverty — an idea later influential in Western thought (the 'Asiatic despotism' / 'Oriental despotism' debate).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Al-Biruni (11th c., Central Asia) = Kitab-ul-Hind (came with Mahmud of Ghazni).
Ibn Battuta (14th c., Morocco) = Rihla; qazi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
François Bernier (17th c., French physician) = Travels in the Mughal Empire.
Bernier claimed no private land ownership in India (crown ownership).
All three wrote outsiders' accounts of Indian society.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Al-Biruni = Kitab-ul-Hind** (came with Mahmud of Ghazni); **Ibn Battuta = Rihla** (Morocco).
**Ibn Battuta served as a qazi under Muhammad bin Tughlaq**.
**Bernier was a French physician** who compared India with Europe.
Bernier wrongly claimed there was **no private property in land** in Mughal India.
